claude_proposed_widenings.name: ReactionTrigger.bearer_misses_attack_roll
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: Peerless Aim fires when the feat holder misses with an attack roll they made. No existing ReactionTrigger variant covers an outgoing miss by the bearer — the current vocabulary only covers incoming events (hit_by_attack_roll, targeted_by_named_spell, creature_casts_spell, spell_save_outcome).
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: When you miss with an attack roll, you can hit instead.

claude_proposed_widenings.name: convert_miss_to_hit
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: Peerless Aim retroactively changes the outcome of the triggering attack roll from a miss to a hit. No existing EffectAtom models outcome override of a resolved attack roll. This is distinct from modify_roll_numeric (adds a bonus before resolution), modify_roll_advantage (changes the roll method), and reroll idioms — it unconditionally flips the binary hit/miss result after the fact.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: When you miss with an attack roll, you can hit instead.

claude_proposed_widenings.name: modify_ability_score with ability: Ability | CastTimeChoice<Ability>
claude_proposed_widenings.justification: The Ability Score Increase sub-feature grants +1 to an ability score of the player's choice (max 30). The current modify_ability_score atom requires a fixed Ability value; it does not support a player-chosen ability. A CastTimeChoice<Ability> extension (paralleling DamageTypeRef = DamageType | CastTimeChoice<DamageType>) would cover this pattern, which recurs across all Epic Boon feats.
claude_proposed_widenings.evidence: Increase one ability score of your choice by 1, to a maximum of 30.
